question: The thick white and yellowish clouds of the planet Venus are made up of which of the following acids?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphuric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The clouds of Venus are primarily composed of droplets of sulphuric acid, along with water vapor and sulfur dioxide.
 
• Sulphuric acid clouds contribute to Venus's extreme greenhouse effect, making it the hottest planet in our solar system.
 
• The high concentration of sulphuric acid in the atmosphere leads to acid rain, though it evaporates before reaching the surface due to the high temperature.
 
• The discovery of sulphuric acid in Venus's atmosphere has been confirmed through various space missions, including those by NASA and the Soviet Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Venus's Atmosphere:**

 
 
• Venus's atmosphere is composed mainly of carbon dioxide (96.5%) and nitrogen (3.5%), with trace amounts of other gases, including sulphur dioxide.
 
• The atmosphere is extremely dense and hot, with surface temperatures reaching up to 465°C (869°F).
 
• The pressure at the surface is about 92 times that of Earth's sea level pressure.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Effect on Venus:**
 
 
• The dense atmosphere of Venus leads to a runaway greenhouse effect, trapping heat and causing extremely high surface temperatures.
 
• The presence of sulphuric acid clouds further enhances this effect by reflecting and absorbing solar radiation.
 
 
 
• **Space Missions to Venus:**
 
 
• Several missions have been sent to Venus to study its atmosphere and surface, including NASA's Magellan and the Soviet Union's Venera program.
 
• The European Space Agency's Venus Express and the Japanese Space Agency's Akatsuki have also provided valuable data on Venus's atmospheric composition and dynamics.
